Commentary.Commentary: So, that completes the formalities of this Test match. The second and final Test between the two sides will begin on 6th August at the same venue. Do join us for that encounter. Until then, it's goodbye from us.

Man of the Match, ROSS TAYLOR says that Wagner bowled very well and the team bowled well from the start. He thinks Zimbabwe will come back hard. For him improvement is necessary and that when you stop improving, its time to retire. It was good for Kane Williamson as it was his first match as captain. He will look to improve and come back again in a few days time. He says it is good to see different part of the world and Zimbabwe is a beautiful country.

Victorious New Zealand skipper, KANE WILLIAMSON says that it might look easy from the scoreboard but Zimbabwe fought very hard and it is a credit to them. After losing the toss on a batting wicket, Williamson says his side did outstandingly well. He says that his boys like to enjoy the game and that is a big part of their culture but on such a big stage they applied themselves. He says that Zimbabwe performed well under pressure and came out hard and will be sticking at it again in the next Test. According to him, the next 9 months will be very busy. With five players off, they will be treasuring every moment of rest but the guys he has with him are fantastic.

GRAEME CREMER admits that it's disappointing to lose although there were some positives. Lauds Williams for his ton although the southpaw was a bit ill. States that it's tough to play in the longest format after a long gap and opines that they didn't adapt better in the second innings after the first innings disaster. Doesn't feel that there would be many changes for the next Test although many players are ill in the dressing room.

Boult's new ball spell on day 3 was exceptional and had Zimbabwe tottering at 17/4. It seemed like the hosts would be rolled over before stumps but their middle order showed some spunk. Raza and Ervine launched a counterattack to surprise the Kiwis although the former departed just before stumps. However, with just 5 wickets left and a deficit of 291 at the start of day 4, the hosts just had too much ground to cover and succumbed albeit with some spunk.

New Zealand's batsmen then complimented their bowlers with a solid batting performance. Latham's century and Williamson's 91 set up the platform for a mammoth score. Taylor conjured a big hundred while Watling too got to the three-figure mark as the duo's unbeaten 253-run stand got the tourists to a commanding 412-run first innings lead. With such a big lead and more than two days left, there was only one way this Test was heading.

The hosts lost the game on the first day itself after putting a meagre total of 164 on the board after opting to bat. Neil Wagner's fifer helped the Kiwis rout the Zimbabwean line-up on a pitch that didn't have many demons on it. The total would have looked embarrassing if not for the resistance by Masvaure and Tiripano after the side were 72/8 at one stage. The duo did take Zimbabwe past the 150-run mark but it was only limiting the damage.

That completes a thumping win for Kiwis as they go 1-0 up in the 2-Test series. The result wasn't in doubt at the start of the day and it was only a matter of when. Sean Williams' entertaining ton and skipper Cremer's defiance delayed the inevitable but couldn't prevent their side from a big defeat. Boult with a 4-fer was the pick of the bowlers in the innings while the others did a decent job.

Welcome back for the second session. GRAEME CREMER and SEAN WILLIAMS to resume their partnership. It shall be ISH SODHI to start proceedings after lunch.
.....DAY 4, SESSION 2.....

New Zealand's bowlers tried hard, particularly the pacers but there wasn't much help off the track barring the odd ball. Southee and Boult extracted some movement but the Zimbabwe batsmen were largely untroubled. The hosts still need another 191 runs to make New Zealand bat again and so the game is still totally under the Kiwis' control. How long can Zimbabwe delay the inevitable? We shall see as the second session begins in a short while.

A good session for Zimbabwe as they scored 100 runs in the 27 overs bowled, losing just the solitary wicket. Ervine departed early in the morning after getting to his fifty but Williams came out all guns blazing to rack up a breezy fifty. Skipper Cremer too dug in there despite enduring several body blows as the pair have stitched an unbeaten 97-run stand of 159 balls to frustrate the Kiwi bowlers.

OUT! GOT HIM! Boult strikes! Good length angled in from around off, straightens a touch after pitching as Ervine pushes at it from the crease. Gets the faintest of edges through to Watling who pouches a good low catch. Break in concentration probably cost Ervine as he had played well yesterday.

Pitched up around off, angled in as Ervine presses forward to block it.
TRENT BOULT to start off from the other end.

Length ball on middle and leg, worked away through mid-wicket for a brace.
THAT WAS CLOSE! Good length just outside off, nips back in sharply as Cremer makes a good leave. That wasn't far away from the off stump.
Maiden Test fifty for CRAIG ERVINE.
Full and tailing into the pads, clipped down to fine leg for a single.
Full and angled away outside off, no stroke offered to that one.
The players and umpires are out on the middle. CRAIG ERVINE and GRAEME CREMER will start the day's batting and TIM SOUTHEE will begin the bowling proceedings.

Raza and Ervine put up a hurried 69-run stand in 53 balls and Zimbabwe looked to be making some headway but Wagner disrupted the partnership by dismissing Raza. Ervine and Cremer are looking steady out there but they still have a 291-run deficit to catch up to. New Zealand will look to continue their devastating attack but Zimbabwe get some much needed rest and come back stronger than yesterday. Join us shortly for the match coverage.

Hello and a warm welcome to day 4 of the 1st Test between Zimbabwe and New Zealand. Yesterday's play saw an all-round commanding performance by the visitors, first dominating with the bat, led by a 253-run stand between Taylor and Watling, and followed by a pace attack led by Boult that washed the Zimbabwean top order away. The Rhodesians are now in a precarious position having lost five wicket and will need to steady the rocking ship.
...Day 4, Session 1...

The batsmen have slowed down a bit and are taking a more measured approach now. While not as fiery, this stand looks to be more sustainable and heralds well for their innings tomorrow. New Zealand, on the other hand, will be sitting pretty on their huge 291-run lead, and will not mind giving away runs in exchange for wickets. Join us tomorrow and find out if the hosts can withstand the visitor's onslaught on day 4. The action will start at 1300 IST! Until then, adios and take care!

New Zealand started the day by impressing with their batting skills and have gone on to put up a commanding performance with the ball as well. Boult picked up three wickets early on and just missed out on his hat-trick. Wagner and Southee distinguished themselves, picking up a wicket apiece.

Zimbabwe were off to a shaky start, the batsmen struggling to remain at the crease as the pacers tore through them. They lost four wickets in 3.3 overs and looked to be in dire straits. That is, until Ervine and Raza stepped in to stabilize the innings. They set up a rapid partnership of 69 runs in 53 balls and looked to be scoring at will. Unfortunately, Raza was taken out by Wagner and the hosts suffered a big set back after losing their fifth wicket. Ervine is on 49 and still at the crease, supported by captain Cremer, and is looking strong.

A lightning session from the hosts. Zimbabwe looked like they had to make up for lost ground and took turns, alternating between scoring rapidly and losing wickets. It was an impressive day for the visitors, with Watling and Taylor lasting for most of the day. After Tea, they carried on their 253-run stand to end the Kiwi innings on a gigantic total of 576-6 and both managed to score centuries. Taylor was unbeaten on 173 and helped set a tall order for the Rhodesians to follow.
